# ztrrfs

> Provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution to a.

<section class="intro">

system of linear equations with a complex triangular coefficient matrix.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ztrrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztrrfs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ztrrfs(
    order,
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N, nrhs,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'`: A is upper triangular; `'lower'`: A is lower triangular. |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the form of the system of equations: `'no-transpose'`: A * X = B (No transpose) `'transpose'`: A**T * X = B (Transpose) `'conjugate-transpose'`: A**H * X = B (Conjugate transpose) |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | in |  | one of `'non-unit'`, `'unit'` | `'non-unit'`: A is non-unit triangular; `'unit'`: A is unit triangular. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | the order of the matrix A. |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | the number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × N` |  | the triangular matrix A. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | the right hand side matrix B. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `B` |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | the solution matrix X. |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `X` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | the estimated forward error bound for each solution vector X(j) (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | the componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector X(j) (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes X(j) an exact solution). |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `2 * N` elements |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `N` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: The triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are also not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: The solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ztrrfs.ndarray(
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N, nrhs,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | `'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'` |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | in |  | one of `'non-unit'`, `'unit'` | `'unit'` or `'non-unit'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand sides |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × N` |  | triangular matrix A, shape [N, N] |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix B, shape [N, nrhs] |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `B` |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix X, shape [N, nrhs] |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `X` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output array of length nrhs for forward error bounds |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output array of length nrhs for backward errors |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | workspace array of length 2*N |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace array of length N |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `RWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `RWORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: The triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are also not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: The solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `RWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetRWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import ztrrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztrrfs';

// 3x3 upper triangular matrix (col-major):
const A = new Complex128Array( [ 2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 1, 0, 0, 3, 1, 5, 2, 6, 1 ] );
const B = new Complex128Array( [ 6, 4, 9, 3, 6, 1 ] );
const X = new Complex128Array( [ 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0 ] );
const FERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const BERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 6 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

const info = ztrrfs.ndarray( 'upper', 'no-transpose', 'non-unit', 3, 1, A, 1, 3, 0, B, 1, 3, 0, X, 1, 3, 0, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );  // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'FERR:', FERR[ 0 ] );  // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'BERR:', BERR[ 0 ] );  // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZTRRFS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZTRRFS provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution to a system of linear equations with a triangular coefficient matrix.

The solution matrix X must be computed by ZTRTRS or some other means before entering this routine. ZTRRFS does not do iterative refinement because doing so cannot improve the backward error.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
